q01: Measure blood lactate in adults with suspected sepsis as an adjunct to clinical assessment.
q02: Obtain blood cultures before administering antimicrobials when this does not substantially delay treatment.
q03: For possible septic shock or a high likelihood of sepsis, give antimicrobials immediately, ideally within 1 hour of recognition.
q04: Give at least 30 mL/kg of intravenous crystalloid within the first 3 hours for sepsis-induced hypoperfusion or septic shock.
q05: Use dynamic measures such as passive leg raise, stroke volume variation, pulse pressure variation, or echocardiography to guide fluid resuscitation.
q06: Target an initial mean arterial pressure of 65 mm Hg in adults with septic shock who are on vasopressors.
q07: Norepinephrine is the first-line vasopressor for septic shock.
q08: Perform source control as soon as feasible after the diagnosis is made.
q09: Consider intravenous corticosteroids for septic shock that is refractory to fluids and vasopressors.
q10: Use a restrictive red blood cell transfusion threshold of hemoglobin below 7 g/dL in adults with sepsis, unless a specific indication exists.
q11: Use low tidal volume ventilation of about 6 mL/kg predicted body weight in sepsis-associated ARDS.
q12: Use prone positioning for at least 12 hours per day in moderate-to-severe ARDS.
q13: Target a glucose level around 144 to 180 mg/dL with insulin in critically ill patients with sepsis.
q14: Use pharmacologic venous thromboembolism prophylaxis, preferably low-molecular-weight heparin, unless contraindicated.
q15: Use renal replacement therapy for sepsis-associated acute kidney injury with metabolic or volume derangements.
q16: Start early enteral nutrition when feasible in critically ill patients with sepsis.
q17: Reassess antimicrobials daily and de-escalate when possible; prefer shorter courses when the infection is controlled.
q18: Admit adults with sepsis or septic shock who require intensive care to the ICU within 6 hours.
q19: Use SBAR to communicate situation, background, assessment, and recommendation to the rapid response team.
q20: A rapid-response page requires a human approval token bound to the alert and patient; the agent cannot page autonomously.
